PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached and no hardware or sim-engine run is claimed. The card's entry symbol robot_sim.envs.basic_env:TaskBaseEnv was verified at robot_sim/envs/basic_env.py:22; the card's family-config/GymnasiumDriver shape fits the real Gymnasium reset/step/action-space interface, so there is no deviation from the card. The upstream environment needs the SAPIEN/ManiSkill2 stack, the initialised submodule and the PartNet-Mobility / GraspNet assets (requirements.txt:3-5; README.md:17-24), package code never imports the clone, and the ManiSkill2 submodule is recorded only as a gitlink in the pinned parent commit, so backends['fake'] is this package's pure Python kinematic stand-in for TaskBaseEnv. The fake models only the Gymnasium surface: action_space, reset(seed, options) and step(action), with the default control mode's flat 11-element action space (base 3 + absolute end-effector pose 6 + gripper 2) and its sourced bounds; it reads no asset and loads no SAPIEN scene. The upstream simulator was therefore not used (its dependencies and assets are not installed here and network installs are forbidden), and the sim backend (gymnasium.make on the class entry point) was not run; it needs the upstream stack, the initialised submodule and the PartNet-Mobility / GraspNet assets (README.md:17-24). NOT COVERED: the 640 x 480 RGB colour arrays from the three cameras (plus their position and segmentation arrays) and the full upstream robot/controller state vector; the fake observation is a smaller 22-float surrogate (11 state values and 11 velocities), while the benchmark configuration observes image mode with three 640 x 480 cameras (robot_sim/config/env/common.yaml:20 and robot_sim/agents/configs/mobile_franka_panda/defaults.py:372-408). NOT COVERED: SAPIEN rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, inverse kinematics, the PartNet-Mobility / GraspNet scene, rendering and snapshot/restore. The fidelity contract describes the deployed fake as F0 engine analytic:RoboCAS-v0 fake, with timestep 100 ms (one control step at the TaskBaseEnv default control_freq 10, robot_sim/envs/basic_env.py:31), determinism seeded, seed_control parameter, lockstep clock and realtime_factor 0; its gaps disclose every difference, including that upstream TaskBaseEnv.evaluate is a stub returning success True (robot_sim/envs/basic_env.py:322-324) so every upstream step terminates (the fake mirrors terminated=True and driver autoreset=True lets the bridge start the next episode), that upstream TaskBaseEnv.set_main_rng discards the seed (robot_sim/envs/basic_env.py:69-70), and that the upstream state observation is richer than the fake's. The fake's initial end-effector pose and jitter are placeholder test data, not facts. Expected warnings kept from the last gate run (no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised): G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 because the seed only arms the next reset and makes no native call; G7.MAYBE_ABSENT x2 for action_space and step because the class-surface reader cannot follow the gitlink submodule that defines the external BaseEnv base, while the names do occur in the clone; G8.NO_UNIT x4 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.values[*] and seed twice. test_driver.py keeps the check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds eight cases (action envelope, step/termination, command echo, different actions, seeded repeat, seed class, fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. Only cap.world.* catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue_requests and no site-limits.example.json is needed; no Limit is declared by the driver (the action envelope is derived from the environment's space) and no bound is operator_required. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
